assertions.title: every shipped image exists, has an allowed licence, an author or credit field, and a Commons source page
assets, texts and characters only reference entities that exist in the database
flags and arms are never shown outside 1836–1936 or outside their recorded period
unqualified symbols of present-day states, peoples, regions and eras were rejected, not shipped
every text carries article, URL, revision and the CC BY-SA licence
linked polities passed the 1836 lifetime check (no silent mismatches)
characters linked to Wikidata agree with the database on birth and death years (±2)
every source id cited by entities, groups and events exists
uses only the five quality labels
a "verified" population total always carries a source; missing data is flagged as a fallback, never verified
covers small states, not only great powers
every map region belongs to exactly one valid owner and is drawn on the map
world population at start is consistent with Maddison (~1.04 bn in 1820, ~1.26 bn in 1850)
records disagreement between sources instead of choosing silently (e.g. Mexico, Portugal, India)
starting heads of state are those in office on 1 Jan 1836
no leader or heir in the starting state took office or was born after the start date
the historical ownership timeline is never applied to the simulation state
initial alliances and wars come from CoW records active on the start date
populations of benchmark groups match their sources
both modes run exactly the same systems the same number of times
mode configuration only toggles historical data layers (no rule or system switches)
AI activity is not reduced in either mode
the historical layer is active only in Historical Mode
mean milestone similarity is higher in Historical Mode than in Sandbox (paired seeds)
Historical Mode does not reproduce history exactly (some milestones are missed)
historical priorities stop applying when their prerequisites disappear
different seeds produce different worlds
wars, alliances, territorial and institutional changes emerge
produces non-historical outcomes (territory changes that differ from the historical owner)
every surviving country — including the smallest — takes AI decisions
a non-historical war declared by the player creates divergence from the AI-only run
Observer Mode rejects player commands (no country under control)
Victoria succeeds William IV in June 1837 and Hanover separates (Salic law)
Sandbox Mode does not use recorded death dates (generated or heir successions only)
is 1.0 at start in both modes (same starting world)
historical: no NaN/negative values in regions and countries
historical: world population growth 1836-1876 is within a plausible band (0.2%-1.2% per year)
historical: national trends stay within a factor of 2 of the 1870 benchmarks (population: CoW; not a script)
sandbox: no NaN/negative values in regions and countries
sandbox: world population growth 1836-1876 is within a plausible band (0.2%-1.2% per year)
sandbox: national trends stay within a factor of 2 of the 1870 benchmarks (population: CoW; not a script)
no law flips back to a value it left within 15 years
wars end: no war lasts more than 12 years
countries keep researching and building over the whole period
a loaded game continues exactly like the uninterrupted game
rejects foreign files
an exhausted attacker that is winning stays in the war
an exhausted attacker that is losing gives up
portrait: no two labels overlap and all stay on screen
portrait: every country name is anchored inside its own country
landscape: no two labels overlap and all stay on screen
landscape: every country name is anchored inside its own country
zoomedOut: no two labels overlap and all stay on screen
zoomedOut: every country name is anchored inside its own country
the player country is labelled at the Europe zoom
every market with prices has per-good supply, demand, imports and shortage after a month
survives save/load, and saves written before the field existed still load
monthly finance lines add up to the income and expense the engine applied
